summary: In Greek mythology, Erato was a dryad who served as the priestess and prophetess of the god Pan; verses were attributed to her at an ancient oracle of Pan located near Acacesium in the territory of Megalopolis, Arcadia. She married Arcas, the son of Zeus and Callisto, and bore him three sons: Azan, Apheidas, and Elatus. She is a distinct figure from the Muse Erato of the same name.
etymology: The name Erato (Ancient Greek: Ἐρατώ) is glossed as "desired" or "lovely."

sections.heading: Name
paragraphs: Her name in Ancient Greek is Ἐρατώ (Eratō), understood to mean "desired" or "lovely".
This Erato, a dryad nymph, shares her name with the Muse Erato, but the two are distinct figures.

sections.heading: Family
paragraphs: Erato was a dryad. She married Arcas, the son of Zeus and Callisto.
By Arcas she bore three sons: Azan, Apheidas, and Elatus.

sections.heading: Mythology
paragraphs: Erato served as the priestess and prophetess of the god Pan.
Verses were attributed to her at an ancient oracle of Pan, located at Megalopolis near Acacesium in Arcadia.
